title: Deathknell trigger target is chosen at resolution instead of when the trigger is finalized onto the chain
expected: trigger-target-lock.ts:85-107 deliberately skips early target locking for non-duplicated triggers: it builds a `duplicated` set of same-card/same-effect trigger keys and `if (duplicated.size === 0) return;` (line 105-107), with the comment "A lone pending trigger is equivalent whether it chooses now or at resolution, and the engine's convention is to prompt at resolution." So a single Ruined Rex Deathknell item is left on the chain with no `targets` and no pendingChoice, and the choose-target prompt is only raised by the damage effect at resolution. Rules 337.1/355.5/383.3 require the Pending triggered item to be Finalized (Game Object chosen) before priority passes (340.4), and 383.4.b.2 targeting-effects depend on that timing, so the "equivalent" assumption is wrong and the observed behavior is a genuine engine deviation.
observed: After Rex died, chain item chain-3 {damage 4, target:{controller:enemy,type:unit}} sat on the chain with no `targets` and pendingChoice=null while passChainPriority was the only move; the choose-target prompt (options = both enemy units) only appeared after priority was passed and the item began resolving
